decision: Increase seismic-monitoring and early-warning investment in Indonesia and the Philippines.
evidence: Strong (M5+) events grew 87% in Indonesia (127 to 238) and 66% in the Philippines (86 to 143), 1 Jan-21 Nov 2026 vs the same period of 2025; both reached M7.8 and are covered by a single (global) network.

decision: Fund regional-network partnerships for high-activity locations covered by only one network.
evidence: 88.1% of 2026 strong events (1,606 of 1,822) occurred in locations reported by a single network - Indonesia, Philippines, Japan, Vanuatu and Tonga lead the list.

decision: Size preparedness and insurance budgets for rare great earthquakes, not for event counts.
evidence: M7+ events are 0.05% of all events but release about 91% of the energy (the M8.8 Kamchatka event of July 2025 alone dominates the 2025 energy total).

decision: Do not treat the +27.5% rise in US event counts as a higher-risk signal.
evidence: The US increase is mostly small events recorded by dense regional networks (59% of Alaska events are below M3); US strong events moved only from 57 to 69.

decision: Label the most recent three weeks of the dashboard as provisional.
evidence: 8.9% of November 2026 events are still automatic (not analyst-reviewed) versus 0.2% in September, so late revisions are expected.
